item.title: Gamers’ Worst Nightmares About AI Are Coming True
item.description: From the global RAM shortage driving up console prices to job loss in the industry, gaming is shaping up to be one of the AI boom's biggest casualties.

item.title: Palantir Demos Show How the Military Could Use AI Chatbots to Generate War Plans
item.description: Software demos and Pentagon records detail how chatbots like Anthropic’s Claude could help the Pentagon analyze intelligence and suggest next steps.

item.title: ‘Uncanny Valley’: Anthropic’s DOD Lawsuit, War Memes, and AI Coming for VC Jobs
item.description: In today’s episode, we discuss how the saga between Anthropic and the Department of Defense is far from over.

item.title: Google Is Not Ruling Out Ads in Gemini
item.description: WIRED spoke with Nick Fox, Google’s SVP of knowledge and information, about how AI is changing the company’s advertising business.

item.title: Google Maps Gets Chatty With a New Gemini-Powered Interface
item.description: “Ask Maps,” rolling out today to Google Maps on mobile, lets you ask Gemini questions about locations and even to plan trips on your behalf.

item.title: Grammarly Is Facing a Class Action Lawsuit Over Its AI ‘Expert Review’ Feature
item.description: The feature, which Grammarly shut down Wednesday, presented editing suggestions as if they came from established authors and academics—without their consent.

item.title: Nvidia Will Spend $26 Billion to Build Open-Weight AI Models, Filings Show
item.description: The move could position the AI infrastructure powerhouse to quickly compete with OpenAI, Anthropic, and DeepSeek.

item.title: Meta Is Developing 4 New Chips to Power Its AI and Recommendation Systems
item.description: The MTIA processors are the tech giant’s latest attempt to build its own AI hardware, even as it continues spending billions on gear from industry leaders like Nvidia.

item.title: This Digital Picture Frame Wants to Bring People Closer to a Holographic Future
item.description: Brooklyn-based Looking Glass has been dabbling in 3D screens for nearly a decade. It's finally launching Musubi, an AI-powered holographic frame to bring your photos and videos to life.

item.title: Nick Clegg Doesn’t Want to Talk About Superintelligence
item.description: After leaving Meta last year, the former deputy prime minister of the UK is charting a new path in the AI industry that has nothing to do with AGI.
